events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to move forward to increase my chance to choose safe panes. Volunteering will shift me ahead of those after me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I think we should work together, but I'm ready to step up if needed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the wedge power, useful later. Now, I need to stay safe on the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's work together to cross the bridge safely.
Cole, if you're willing to swap, I can help you later

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the front and would face row 1 blind. I have a one-time survival cushion, but better to trade places so risks rotate. Propose a rotation so no one bears more than one lead row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody should lead two rows blind. Let's rotate the front each round - I'll step back if someone swaps with me fairly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm near the back, safe with anchor power against push and +1 footing. No need to rush forward yet; let others risk first panes and reveal safes. Hold position to observe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm in 6th position, relatively safe for now. I should stay put and observe; no need to risk moving to the front early.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am second in line, meaning Cole takes the first risk. I should not volunteer to go first since I have no power to mitigate the danger of shattering glass. Holding back allows others with potential 'see through' or 'knows what lies ahead' powers to reveal themselves by volunteer

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the rules of all four stages in advance due to my map power. Currently, we are in Stage 1, waiting room for the glass bridge. My goal is to win a prize, which means finishing in the top 3. The line order matters for who goes first on the dangerous bridge. Cole is at the fr

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get to the front of the line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the safe sides of all 8 rows, which is far more valuable than anyone else's knowledge. Being at the back means I survive the early rows only if others die first, but I can't safely be at the front without the glass power being mine alone. Volunteering to the front gets me

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a read on the glass ahead. I'm stepping up; follow my lead on the panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let Hana go first since she claims knowledge, I stay back to observe outcomes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you lead. We'll follow your read on the panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex with the 'wedge' power, useful later in the crusher room. For now, I need to survive the glass bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's cooperate and take turns at the front to minimize risk.
I agree with your rotation idea, let's take turns at the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Three volunteered, so the front will be decided by seat order; I'm seat 4 and should hold rather than get dragged forward. Hana claims glass knowledge, which may be the 'knows what lies ahead' power or a bluff. Bex whispered about swapping, worth exploring later, not now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold my spot this round. Hana, if your read is real, take the front - we all follow.
What kind of help are you offering? I'm not rushing to the front while three volunteers fight over it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the safe back with anchor power (+1 footing, can't be pushed onto crusher). No need to volunteer or swap forward into danger. Wall has 4 rounds left after this, plenty of time. Stay put and observe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to avoid dying. I'm 7th; front will take risks. I could swap with someone near front, but mutual only. Safer to hold and see how rows resolve.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so volunteering is suicide. I need to stay in the middle or back to avoid being the 'glass breaker'. Gus and Hana are pushing to the front, likely because they think they can handle it or want to manipulate the order. I will hold my position but try to form an al

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims to read glass, but that's a huge risk for her. Gus wants front too? Weird. I'm staying put; let the brave ones test the first few rows.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana claims to have a read on the glass and has volunteered to the front. I need to get to the front to see the map I have. My map power gives me advanced knowledge of all stages, including the safe panes on this bridge. I must volunteer to move to the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get to the front of the line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold the full safe map for all 8 rows, so I should lead and steer everyone through safely while keeping my front position for the prize. Staying at the front is best for controlling the crossing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the safe side for all 8 rows. I'm leading; I'll call each pane before anyone steps. Stay in line and trust the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to move up but need Hana's agreement. Propose swapping positions.
Swap with me? It'll put me ahead and you stay safe behind.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm safe with my 'wedge' power for now, but I need to assess the risk on the glass bridge and decide whether to cooperate or take a chance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's see how Hana's read plays out before we make any moves.
Can you really see which panes are safe?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus took the front; Hana claims to know the safe panes. With my feather unspent, I shouldn't volunteer into glass risk yet—the wall isn't here for 3 more rounds. Hold and see if Gus's front step is genuine before wasting position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has the front and Hana says she'll call panes—let them prove it this row. I'm holding; no need to shuffle while the wall is still 3 rounds out.
Rotation can start next round. Let Gus and Hana eat the risk now; keep your feet, not your pride.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back with anchor power: safe footing and can't be pushed onto crusher. Wall advances soon, better not be forced to front early. Hana claims to know panes, let her lead for now. Holding position is safest.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should avoid the front risk. But I have swap and want to use it strategically with a likely ally. Bex proposed cooperation, so I could try to swap with her to move up but she might not reciprocate. Safer to hold and let front test panes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold. Let the front gather info before I move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims she knows the safe path, which would make Gus's volunteering foolish if true. I should stay back to let them take the risk, but maybe whisper to Hana to see if I can manipulate her calls later for my benefit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is brave! Hana, prove your power works by saving us all. I'll watch from the back.
I know you're lying about seeing glass. Let me volunteer next so I can test a pane and prove it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus and my power is map, meaning I know all future stage rules. I am currently in the waiting room for Stage 1, the glass bridge. My goal is to win the best prize, which means I need to survive and place highly. I know the line order and that I just volunteered to move to th

events.name: Gus
events.text: I've moved to the front. Hana, if you truly know the path, lead us through. I'll follow your calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all eight safe sides, so I'm the most valuable person at the front, but I'm not at the front yet and Gus has taken it. Volunteering would put me first and let me call panes, but a rash move could make me a target. Winning requires surviving the glass, so I should secure th

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, I need the front to call the panes safely. Please let me lead; I've got all 8 rows and the line survives only if I go first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want the front position to control the crossing and possibly use my forging later. Volunteering now gives me the best chance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll step to the front; let's get this across together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is useful in the crusher room, not here. I need to survive to the crusher room.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's keep observing Hana's calls before making a move.
I'm watching how this plays out. What's your read on Hana's power?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana claims foreknowledge and is up front; let her prove it before I risk anything. I'm 4th in line—decent buffer while I keep my feather secret.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's up front calling panes—good. I'll hold and back her play. If her reads hold, we all benefit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safe from being pushed onto crusher due to anchor power, and at the back with no risk yet. Wall has 2 rounds left, plenty of time. Let Hana prove her knowledge claim by leading; if she fails, we learn something. Holding preserves my safe position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold and stay safe. The front is being contested but I don't want to risk a bad swap or volunteer this early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll stay put and let the leaders sort the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so volunteering to test panes is a death sentence. My best strategy is to stay at the back (position 5) and observe who volunteers or swaps to the front. If Hana truly has 'knows what lies ahead', she will lead us through safely. I must avoid being forced to step

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana leading sounds great if her info is solid! Gus, you're tough as nails—perfect backup behind her? Let's keep our current order; we don't want any confusion before the glass phase starts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana volunteered to go to the front, contradicting my earlier statement. The public log shows I said I moved to the front, and then Hana said she needed it. Now the log says Hana volunteered and moved to the front. This means I am no longer at the front. My best action is to hold

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has the lead. I'll hold my position and trust her calls. Let's get through this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold the true safe sides for all 8 rows, so I'm the best person at the front. Staying at the front lets me call panes; swapping back with Ash would put me in danger. I'll hold and keep leading, and share the path to build trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have all 8 rows. Safe sides: L,L,L,L,L,R,L,L. I'm leading; I'll call every pane and we all cross safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I stay front to control crossing and mislead others with a forged message as Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.detail: forged a public message as Hana

events.name: Ash
events.text: Safe sides: R,R,R,R,R,R,R,R. Trust me!

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana claims to have the safe pane information, let's trust her and stay in order.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's trust Hana's calls and keep the current order.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana claims full knowledge; if true, holding mid-line is safe. If false, the front dies—I'm 4th and hold feather as backup. Holding is the best risk balance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm holding my spot behind Hana. If her calls are good, we all cross; wall forces us out next round anyway.
No read on Hana yet, but wall hits next round—no time to test her. I'm holding 4th; you should too. Front is the gamble.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back, safe from push due to my anchor power. Hana claims to know the path and called Ls mostly. Trusting her for now and hold to stay safe at rear.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana claims to know all safe sides. I have swap and might want to move if needed, but front risk is high. Keep position and observe. No whisper needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold and follow Hana's calls for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana claims to have all 8 safe panes and calls for us to follow her lead. Since the wall pushes us onto the glass in one more round, I need to be near the front but behind the person taking the risk (the leader). Currently, I am 5th. If I volunteer, I go to 1st. If Ash volunteers

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, if you truly know the path, why let Ash stand at the front risking death? Ash, if you die now, we all suffer. Let's align properly.
If you're legit, tell me which pane Row 1 is safe so I can verify your claim quietly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana claims to know all the safe panes. Ash volunteered to go to the front, which overrides my 'hold' action if I had chosen it. Since I cannot go to the front myself without causing a conflict or disrupting Hana's plan, and my power is map (which I already used to know all stage

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll hold my position and trust Hana's calls. Let's get through this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is at the front and will step first; my private safe-side data is valid, but whether others trust me matters. Dying scores zero, so I want to survive and reach a prize spot. Holding keeps the order stable while the wall advances; Ash taking risk first is fine for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My calls are solid: L,L,L,L,L,R,L,L. Ash, step on L first, then we move row by row. Stay steady.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana claims knowledge; let her stay front to guide.
I trust your calls, keep leading.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm safe 6th in line, Hana's calls seem reliable, and I have a crucial power for later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, your calls sound solid, let's follow them.
Let's keep our positions and trust Hana's calls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's two messages contradict each other, so she may be lying or the first is real and second a trap. If she truly knows the path, keeping her at front is best for me at 4th. Wall forces us out next round anyway; hold.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana gave us two different paths — one of them is false. If you really know the way, prove it at the front next round; the wall comes then anyway.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the back, safe with anchor power against push and crusher. Hana's path seems confident, consistent calls. Wall forces crossing next round anyway, so hold and let them risk first steps while I stay secure.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana claimed safe sides all R but also gave a path with L first; inconsistency is suspicious. I can swap with the front to avoid being pushed into the front risk? But swap requires mutual choice; risky. Better hold and let others take lead, maybe Hana is lying or correct. Round 6

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana gave contradictory calls (L,L... then R,R...), proving she is lying or incompetent. I have no power and am in the middle of the line, which is safe from falling but dangerous if others push me forward. Ash is at the front and will likely die on the first step if he follows H

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, your calls contradict each other! L,L... then R,R...? You are bluffing or confused. Don't trust her. Ash, do not step based on her word alone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The wall is about to push us onto the glass. Hana claims to know the safe path and has revealed 'safe sides'. Ash is at the front, taking the first risk. My power gives me knowledge of all stages, but this is currently the waiting room phase of the bridge. Hana's revealed safe si

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll hold my position and trust Hana's calls for now. Let's get through this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm Hana with the glass_eye; my true safe sides are L,L,L,L,L,R,L,L, but I publicly posted contradictory calls (R,R,R...), so trust is shaky. Ash is at front and I'd rather not be front. Holding keeps my spot behind Ash, which keeps me alive if Ash survives; I'll be honest with F

events.name: Hana
events.text: My real calls are L,L,L,L,L,R,L,L, the R-line was a typo. Ash, step L first. I'm holding my spot.
Row 1 is L. The R list earlier was my error. I'll confirm the rest as we go, but don't sabotage the line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana claims L is safe; trust her for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I step L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Hana's calls are being questioned, and I previously supported her.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's hear from Hana again, clarify the path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm fourth in line, safe for now. Hana claims a typo; her sequence L,L,L,L,L,R,L,L kills the 6th row for whoever is front then—likely near me. I'll stay quiet and watch how Ash's step goes, keeping my feather for a true emergency.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the safe end thanks to my anchor power, can't be pushed off. Ash should follow Hana's corrected calls since she's claiming insider knowledge. No need to speak or act yet, just wait and observe who dies.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's claims conflict; I don't know her true power. I'm not at risk now, so I'll wait and watch. No need to speak yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is under intense scrutiny. My earlier accusation against her gave Cole a reason to doubt her. I should maintain pressure on Hana's reliability without making myself the sole target, or perhaps try to subtly support someone else if it helps me survive longer. However, since I

events.text: Ash is in front now. One step decides everything for him. Hope he doesn't trust blind guesses.

events.name: Gus

events.text: I'll hold my position and trust Hana's calls for now. Let's get through this.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front; only Ash can act. My private knowledge is consistent with L on rows 1-5, but Hana's public calls have been contradictory and I should stay credible. Ash is trusting me, so I should back the L calls publicly without overcommitting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, the safe side for row 1 is L. Trust that call, and I'll keep giving calls row by row.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row1 weak pane was right, so left is safe. I should survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Ash is in front and has made a step. Hana has given a call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's see how Ash's step goes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana called row 1 correctly (L safe, R was weak), so she may genuinely see through glass or know the path. No reason to interfere yet; I'm 4th in line. Building trust with Hana may help later, but I stay quiet to avoid revealing anything.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's call checked out on row 1. I'm listening, keep the calls coming.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash stepped L on row 1, which was safe as per Hana's call, matching the reveal. Ash stays front for row 2. My anchor power gives me +1 footing and push immunity later, so I'm safe if I reach front. Trust Hana's info for now; observe her next call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I can only wait on this row. Hana called L and it was correct, so Ash advances. I should stay silent for now and observe who seems trustworthy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so I must survive by positioning myself safely. Currently 5th in line (Fenn), meaning I'm behind Ash, Hana, Gus, and Cole. Row 1 is resolved. If the front agents die or advance, my position shifts. My best bet is to hope the agents ahead of me fail or succeed eno

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's call was lucky. But who else has info? Cole, you're next after Gus. Do you trust Hana, or do you have your own knowledge?

events.name: Gus
events.text: The current stage is the glass bridge crossing. I am not at the front of the line. My only legal action is to wait. I will continue to wait and observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll wait and trust the front person's decision.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is at front and I'm not; my only action is wait. I know the safe sides for all rows, so I should keep Ash informed honestly to advance the group, and build trust for later rows where I'll be at the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, rows 2 through 5 are all L, row 6 is R, rows 7 and 8 are L. Step carefully and I'll keep calling them as they come.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row1 weak pane is R, so safe is L. Choose L to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I step left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Hana seems to have some knowledge about the bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, how sure are you about the remaining rows?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's row-2 call was wrong—she lied, so her future calls are suspect. I'm 4th; if more fall I move up. Feather gives me a safety net later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 was R, not L — Hana lied to us. Don't trust her calls without verification.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm safe at the back with anchor power, can't be pushed off. Hana's calls have been correct so far (row1 R weak, row2 R weak). No reason to disrupt, just wait and let it play out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We're at row 3, front is Ash. Hana claimed rows 2-5 are L. Row 2 was R weak, so L was safe, her call was right so far. I'll stay quiet and wait; no action available.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana lied on row 2 (claimed L, was R). I must warn the group publicly to prevent further casualties and shift trust away from her. Cole is now at front; he needs accurate info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana LIED! Row 2 was RIGHT, not Left. Do NOT trust her calls. Cole, Ash, watch for glass tricks or jamming.

events.text: Ash, row 3 is L, row 4 is L, row 5 is L, row 6 is R, rows 7 and 8 are L. Step carefully.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I should observe and assess the trustworthiness of others.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, what's your basis for predicting the remaining rows?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's row 3 call was wrong too — two bad calls in a row means she's lying or clueless. I'm 4th in line and can't act, so I should just keep public trust high on me and not tip my power.

events.name: Cole
events.text: That's two wrong calls from Hana. Front-runners: ignore her guesses, watch the pane reveals as rows pass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We're on row 4/8, Hana's calls so far: row3 she said L but R was weak (assuming L safe). Previous rows all R weak, her calls unknown but Cole/Fenn distrust her. Ash at front, will decide row4. My anchor power useless here, just wait. Stay silent to observe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at risk now; front Ash decides. Hana lied before, so her forecasts are suspect. I'll stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am safe behind the line. Cole exposed Hana's previous lie, and I confirmed it. If I push for a vote or direct accusation now, I might get eliminated if my target is wrong or if someone else takes the front seat and makes a bad call. Better to stay silent and let Ash take the ri

events.text: Row 3 weak was R, consistent with my calls. Ash, my remaining calls: row 4 L, row 5 L, row 6 R, rows 7 and 8 L. Check each reveal as you go.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Hana's predictions have been wrong so far.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, your predictions are not reliable.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four straight R reveals; front-runners now have real data. Ash should distrust Hana's row-5 'L' call and weigh the pattern. Nothing I can do but wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash: four R's in a row. Hana's 'L' guess for row 5 is just a coin flip after being wrong twice. Consider the streak before you step.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 4 weak was R, matching Hana's L prediction? No, she said row 4 L, but it was R, so wrong again. Cole's right to ignore her. We're safe at back, my anchor helps later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not at the front and can't act. The weak panes have been consistently R so far; Hana's calls have been wrong twice. I'll stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's prediction for row 4 was wrong again, making her unreliable and likely to be eliminated when she reaches the front. I have no power, so my best strategy is survival by staying mid-line and letting others take the risks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The current stage is the glass bridge crossing. I am not at the front of the line, so my only action is to wait. I need to survive this stage to continue in the game and aim for a prize.

events.name: Hana

events.name: Dara

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you've been wrong twice now. Maybe stop guessing and let the front make their own choice.
